title: A Review of the Clinical Effects of Psychotomimetic Agents
author: Humphry Osmond
summary: Osmond surveyed psychotomimetic agents and proposed new terminologies, settling on "psychedelic, mind-manifesting" as his choice. This paper put the word into circulation among psychiatrists, coining the term still used today.
excerpt: "My choice, because it is clear, euphonious, and uncontaminated by other associations, is psychedelic, mind-manifesting."
citation: Humphry Osmond, "A Review of the Clinical Effects of Psychotomimetic Agents," Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences 66, no. 3 (March 1957): 418–434.
rights: In copyright (Wiley, for the New York Academy of Sciences). No US Government interest.

draft.rationale: The single most important terminological document in the archive's period: the paper that coined "psychedelic." Delivered to a New York Academy of Sciences conference and drawing on roughly fifty administrations of LSD and mescaline to volunteers (including Aldous Huxley). Osmond argued that "psychotomimetic" was too narrow and pathologizing, proposing several alternative coinages (psychehormic, psycherhexic, psychezymic, psychelytic) before settling on psychedelic. Directly continues the Osmond-Smythies 1952 biochemical research program and Osmond-Hoffer-Smythies threads.
